android.app.state.brief: This attribute represents the state of the application.

android.os.api_level.brief: Uniquely identifies the framework API revision offered by a version (`os.version`) of the Android operating system. More information can be found in the [Android API levels documentation](https://developer.android.com/guide/topics/manifest/uses-sdk-element#ApiLevels).

app.build_id.brief: Unique identifier for a particular build or compilation of the application.

app.crash.id.brief: A unique identifier representing an instance of an end user facing app crash.

app.installation.id.brief: A unique identifier representing the installation of an application on a specific device

app.jank.frame_count.brief: A number of frame renders that experienced jank.

app.jank.period.brief: The time period, in seconds, for which this jank is being reported.

app.jank.threshold.brief: The minimum rendering threshold for this jank, in seconds.

app.screen.coordinate.x.brief: The x (horizontal) coordinate of a screen coordinate, in screen pixels.

app.screen.coordinate.y.brief: The y (vertical) component of a screen coordinate, in screen pixels.

app.screen.id.brief: An identifier that uniquely differentiates this screen from other screens in the same application.

app.screen.name.brief: The name of an application screen.

app.widget.id.brief: An identifier that uniquely differentiates this widget from other widgets in the same application.

app.widget.name.brief: The name of an application widget.

artifact.attestation.filename.brief: The provenance filename of the built attestation which directly relates to the build artifact filename. This filename SHOULD accompany the artifact at publish time. See the [SLSA Relationship](https://slsa.dev/spec/v1.0/distributing-provenance#relationship-between-artifacts-and-attestations) specification for more information.

artifact.attestation.hash.brief: The full [hash value (see glossary)](https://nvlpubs.nist.gov/nistpubs/FIPS/NIST.FIPS.186-5.pdf), of the built attestation. Some envelopes in the [software attestation space](https://github.com/in-toto/attestation/tree/main/spec) also refer to this as the **digest**.

artifact.filename.brief: The human readable filename of the artifact, typically generated during build and release processes. Often includes the package name and version in the filename.

artifact.hash.brief: The full [hash value (see glossary)](https://nvlpubs.nist.gov/nistpubs/FIPS/NIST.FIPS.186-5.pdf), often found in checksum.txt on a release of the artifact and used to verify package integrity.

artifact.purl.brief: The [Package URL](https://github.com/package-url/purl-spec) of the [package artifact](https://slsa.dev/spec/v1.0/terminology#package-model) provides a standard way to identify and locate the packaged artifact.

aspnetcore.authentication.result.brief: The result of the authentication operation.

aspnetcore.authentication.scheme.brief: The identifier that names a particular authentication handler.

aspnetcore.authorization.policy.brief: The name of the authorization policy.

aspnetcore.authorization.result.brief: The result of calling the authorization service.

aspnetcore.diagnostics.exception.result.brief: ASP.NET Core exception middleware handling result.

aspnetcore.diagnostics.handler.type.brief: Full type name of the [`IExceptionHandler`](https://learn.microsoft.com/dotnet/api/microsoft.aspnetcore.diagnostics.iexceptionhandler) implementation that handled the exception.

aspnetcore.identity.error_code.brief: The error code for a failed identity operation.

aspnetcore.identity.password_check_resul.brief: The result from checking the password.

aspnetcore.identity.result.brief: The result of the identity operation.

aspnetcore.identity.sign_in.result.brief: Whether the sign in result was success or failure.

aspnetcore.identity.token_purpose.brief: What the token will be used for.

aspnetcore.identity.user_type.brief: The full name of the identity user type.

aspnetcore.memory_pool.owner.brief: The name of the library or subsystem using the memory pool instance.

aspnetcore.rate_limiting.result.brief: Rate-limiting result, shows whether the lease was acquired or contains a rejection reason

aspnetcore.request.is_unhandled.brief: Flag indicating if request was handled by the application pipeline.

aspnetcore.routing.is_fallback.brief: A value that indicates whether the matched route is a fallback route.

aspnetcore.sign_in.is_persistent.brief: A flag indicating whether the sign in is persistent.

aspnetcore.user.is_authenticated.brief: A value that indicates whether the user is authenticated.

aws.bedrock.guardrail.id.brief: The unique identifier of the AWS Bedrock Guardrail. A [guardrail](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/guardrails.html) helps safeguard and prevent unwanted behavior from model responses or user messages.

aws.bedrock.knowledge_base.id.brief: The unique identifier of the AWS Bedrock Knowledge base. A [knowledge base](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/knowledge-base.html) is a bank of information that can be queried by models to generate more relevant responses and augment prompts.

aws.dynamodb.attribute_definitions.brief: The JSON-serialized value of each item in the `AttributeDefinitions` request field.

aws.dynamodb.attributes_to_get.brief: The value of the `AttributesToGet` request parameter.

aws.dynamodb.consistent_read.brief: The value of the `ConsistentRead` request parameter.

aws.dynamodb.consumed_capacity.brief: The JSON-serialized value of each item in the `ConsumedCapacity` response field.

aws.dynamodb.count.brief: The value of the `Count` response parameter.

aws.dynamodb.exclusive_start_table.brief: The value of the `ExclusiveStartTableName` request parameter.

aws.dynamodb.global_secondary_index_upda.brief: The JSON-serialized value of each item in the `GlobalSecondaryIndexUpdates` request field.

aws.dynamodb.global_secondary_indexes.brief: The JSON-serialized value of each item of the `GlobalSecondaryIndexes` request field

aws.dynamodb.index_name.brief: The value of the `IndexName` request parameter.

aws.dynamodb.item_collection_metrics.brief: The JSON-serialized value of the `ItemCollectionMetrics` response field.

aws.dynamodb.limit.brief: The value of the `Limit` request parameter.

aws.dynamodb.local_secondary_indexes.brief: The JSON-serialized value of each item of the `LocalSecondaryIndexes` request field.

aws.dynamodb.projection.brief: The value of the `ProjectionExpression` request parameter.

aws.dynamodb.provisioned_read_capacity.brief: The value of the `ProvisionedThroughput.ReadCapacityUnits` request parameter.

aws.dynamodb.provisioned_write_capacity.brief: The value of the `ProvisionedThroughput.WriteCapacityUnits` request parameter.

aws.dynamodb.scan_forward.brief: The value of the `ScanIndexForward` request parameter.

aws.dynamodb.scanned_count.brief: The value of the `ScannedCount` response parameter.

aws.dynamodb.segment.brief: The value of the `Segment` request parameter.

aws.dynamodb.select.brief: The value of the `Select` request parameter.

aws.dynamodb.table_count.brief: The number of items in the `TableNames` response parameter.

aws.dynamodb.table_names.brief: The keys in the `RequestItems` object field.

aws.dynamodb.total_segments.brief: The value of the `TotalSegments` request parameter.

aws.ecs.container.arn.brief: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of an [ECS container instance](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonECS/latest/developerguide/ECS_instances.html).

aws.ecs.task.family.brief: The family name of the [ECS task definition](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonECS/latest/developerguide/task_definitions.html) used to create the ECS task.

aws.ecs.task.id.brief: The ID of a running ECS task. The ID MUST be extracted from `task.arn`.

aws.ecs.task.revision.brief: The revision for the task definition used to create the ECS task.

aws.eks.cluster.arn.brief: The ARN of an EKS cluster.

aws.extended_request_id.brief: The AWS extended request ID as returned in the response header `x-amz-id-2`.

aws.kinesis.stream_name.brief: The name of the AWS Kinesis [stream](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/streams/latest/dev/introduction.html) the request refers to. Corresponds to the `--stream-name` parameter of the Kinesis [describe-stream](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/cli/latest/reference/kinesis/describe-stream.html) operation.

aws.lambda.invoked_arn.brief: The full invoked ARN as provided on the `Context` passed to the function (`Lambda-Runtime-Invoked-Function-Arn` header on the `/runtime/invocation/next` applicable).

aws.lambda.resource_mapping.id.brief: The UUID of the [AWS Lambda EvenSource Mapping](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSCloudFormation/latest/UserGuide/aws-resource-lambda-eventsourcemapping.html). An event source is mapped to a lambda function. It's contents are read by Lambda and used to trigger a function. This isn't available in the lambda execution context or the lambda runtime environment. This is going to be populated by the AWS SDK for each language when that UUID is present. Some of these operations are Create/Delete/Get/List/Update EventSourceMapping.

aws.log.group.arns.brief: The Amazon Resource Name(s) (ARN) of the AWS log group(s).

aws.log.group.names.brief: The name(s) of the AWS log group(s) an application is writing to.

aws.log.stream.arns.brief: The ARN(s) of the AWS log stream(s).

aws.log.stream.names.brief: The name(s) of the AWS log stream(s) an application is writing to.

aws.request_id.brief: The AWS request ID as returned in the response headers `x-amzn-requestid`, `x-amzn-request-id` or `x-amz-request-id`.

aws.s3.bucket.brief: The S3 bucket name the request refers to. Corresponds to the `--bucket` parameter of the [S3 API](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/cli/latest/reference/s3api/index.html) operations.

aws.s3.copy_source.brief: The source object (in the form `bucket`/`key`) for the copy operation.

aws.s3.delete.brief: The delete request container that specifies the objects to be deleted.

aws.s3.key.brief: The S3 object key the request refers to. Corresponds to the `--key` parameter of the [S3 API](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/cli/latest/reference/s3api/index.html) operations.

aws.s3.part_number.brief: The part number of the part being uploaded in a multipart-upload operation. This is a positive integer between 1 and 10,000.

aws.s3.upload_id.brief: Upload ID that identifies the multipart upload.

aws.secretsmanager.secret.arn.brief: The ARN of the Secret stored in the Secrets Manager

aws.sns.topic.arn.brief: The ARN of the AWS SNS Topic. An Amazon SNS [topic](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/sns/latest/dg/sns-create-topic.html) is a logical access point that acts as a communication channel.

aws.sqs.queue.url.brief: The URL of the AWS SQS Queue. It's a unique identifier for a queue in Amazon Simple Queue Service (SQS) and is used to access the queue and perform actions on it.

aws.step_functions.activity.arn.brief: The ARN of the AWS Step Functions Activity.

aws.step_functions.state_machine.arn.brief: The ARN of the AWS Step Functions State Machine.

az.client_request_id.brief: Value of the `x-ms-client-request-id` header the SDK sent with the request.

az.schema_url.brief: OpenTelemetry semantic-convention schema URL the Azure SDK's own span attributes conform to.

azure.client.id.brief: The unique identifier of the client instance.

azure.cosmosdb.operation.contacted_regio.brief: List of regions contacted during operation in the order that they were contacted. If there is more than one region listed, it indicates that the operation was performed on multiple regions i.e. cross-regional call.

azure.cosmosdb.operation.request_charge.brief: The number of request units consumed by the operation.

azure.resource_group.name.brief: The name of the Azure [resource group](https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/azure-resource-manager/management/manage-resource-groups-portal) the resource belongs to.

azure.resource_provider.namespace.brief: [Azure Resource Provider Namespace](https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/azure-resource-manager/management/azure-services-resource-providers) as recognized by the client.

azure.service.request.id.brief: The unique identifier of the service request. It's generated by the Azure service and returned with the response.

browser.brands.brief: Array of brand name and version separated by a space

browser.document.url.full.brief: Absolute URL of the current browser document according to [RFC3986](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc3986).

browser.language.brief: Preferred language of the user using the browser

browser.mobile.brief: A boolean that is true if the browser is running on a mobile device

browser.platform.brief: The platform on which the browser is running

browser.web_vital.delta.brief: The delta between the current value and the last-reported value. See [delta](https://github.com/GoogleChrome/web-vitals?tab=readme-ov-file#report-only-the-delta-of-changes).

browser.web_vital.id.brief: A unique ID representing this particular metric instance.

browser.web_vital.navigation_type.brief: The type of navigation, as reported by the [Navigation Timing API](https://developer.mozilla.org/docs/Web/API/PerformanceNavigationTiming/type), with additional values reported by the web-vitals library.

browser.web_vital.rating.brief: The rating of the web vital value against the "good", "needs improvement", and "poor" thresholds defined for the metric.

build.error.message.brief: Message of the exception that failed building the workflow.

build.error.type.brief: Full type name of the exception that failed building the workflow.

cassandra.consistency.level.brief: The consistency level of the query. Based on consistency values from [CQL](https://docs.datastax.com/en/cassandra-oss/3.0/cassandra/dml/dmlConfigConsistency.html).

cassandra.coordinator.dc.brief: The data center of the coordinating node for a query.

cassandra.coordinator.id.brief: The ID of the coordinating node for a query.

cassandra.page.size.brief: The fetch size used for paging, i.e. how many rows will be returned at once.

cassandra.query.idempotent.brief: Whether or not the query is idempotent.

cassandra.speculative_execution.count.brief: The number of times a query was speculatively executed. Not set or `0` if the query was not executed speculatively.

cicd.pipeline.action.name.brief: The kind of action a pipeline run is performing.

cicd.pipeline.name.brief: The human readable name of the pipeline within a CI/CD system.

cicd.pipeline.result.brief: The result of a pipeline run.

cicd.pipeline.run.id.brief: The unique identifier of a pipeline run within a CI/CD system.

cicd.pipeline.run.state.brief: The pipeline run goes through these states during its lifecycle.

cicd.pipeline.run.url.full.brief: The [URL](https://wikipedia.org/wiki/URL) of the pipeline run, providing the complete address in order to locate and identify the pipeline run.

cicd.pipeline.task.name.brief: The human readable name of a task within a pipeline. Task here most closely aligns with a [computing process](https://wikipedia.org/wiki/Pipeline_(computing)) in a pipeline. Other terms for tasks include commands, steps, and procedures.

cicd.pipeline.task.run.id.brief: The unique identifier of a task run within a pipeline.

cicd.pipeline.task.run.result.brief: The result of a task run.

cicd.pipeline.task.run.url.full.brief: The [URL](https://wikipedia.org/wiki/URL) of the pipeline task run, providing the complete address in order to locate and identify the pipeline task run.

cicd.pipeline.task.type.brief: The type of the task within a pipeline.

cicd.system.component.brief: The name of a component of the CI/CD system.

cicd.worker.id.brief: The unique identifier of a worker within a CI/CD system.

cicd.worker.name.brief: The name of a worker within a CI/CD system.

cicd.worker.state.brief: The state of a CI/CD worker / agent.

cicd.worker.url.full.brief: The [URL](https://wikipedia.org/wiki/URL) of the worker, providing the complete address in order to locate and identify the worker.

client.address.brief: Client address - domain name if available without reverse DNS lookup; otherwise, IP address or UNIX domain socket name.

cloud.account.id.brief: The cloud account ID the resource is assigned to.

cloud.availability_zone.brief: Cloud regions often have multiple, isolated locations known as zones to increase availability. Availability zone represents the zone where the resource is running.

cloud.region.brief: The AWS Region where the requested service is being accessed.

cloud.resource_id.brief: Cloud provider-specific native identifier of the monitored cloud resource (e.g. an [ARN](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/general/latest/gr/aws-arns-and-namespaces.html) on AWS, a [fully qualified resource ID](https://learn.microsoft.com/rest/api/resources/resources/get-by-id) on Azure, a [full resource name](https://google.aip.dev/122#full-resource-names) on GCP)

cloudfoundry.app.instance.id.brief: The index of the application instance. 0 when just one instance is active.

cloudfoundry.org.id.brief: The guid of the CloudFoundry org the application is running in.

cloudfoundry.org.name.brief: The name of the CloudFoundry organization the app is running in.

cloudfoundry.space.id.brief: The guid of the CloudFoundry space the application is running in.

cloudfoundry.space.name.brief: The name of the CloudFoundry space the application is running in.

cloudfoundry.system.id.brief: A guid or another name describing the event source.

cloudfoundry.system.instance.id.brief: A guid describing the concrete instance of the event source.

code.namespace.brief: Deprecated, namespace is now included into `code.function.name`

container.command.brief: The command used to run the container (i.e. the command name).

container.command_args.brief: All the command arguments (including the command/executable itself) run by the container.

container.command_line.brief: The full command run by the container as a single string representing the full command.

container.csi.plugin.name.brief: The name of the CSI ([Container Storage Interface](https://github.com/container-storage-interface/spec)) plugin used by the volume.

container.csi.volume.id.brief: The unique volume ID returned by the CSI ([Container Storage Interface](https://github.com/container-storage-interface/spec)) plugin.

container.id.brief: Container ID. Usually a UUID, as for example used to [identify Docker containers](https://docs.docker.com/engine/containers/run/#container-identification). The UUID might be abbreviated.

container.image.id.brief: Runtime specific image identifier. Usually a hash algorithm followed by a UUID.

container.image.name.brief: Name of the image the container was built on.

container.image.repo_digests.brief: Repository digests of the container image as provided by the container runtime.

container.image.tags.brief: Container image tags. An example can be found in [Docker Image Inspect](https://docs.docker.com/reference/api/engine/version/v1.52/#tag/Image/operation/ImageInspect). Should be only the `<tag>` section of the full name for example from `registry.example.com/my-org/my-image:<tag>`.

container.label.brief: Container labels, `<key>` being the label name, the value being the label value.

container.name.brief: Container name used by container runtime.

container.runtime.brief: The container runtime managing this container.

container.runtime.description.brief: A description about the runtime which could include, for example details about the CRI/API version being used or other customizations.

container.runtime.name.brief: The container runtime managing this container.

container.runtime.version.brief: The version of the runtime of this process, as returned by the runtime without modification.

cpython.gc.generation.brief: Value of the garbage collector collection generation.

db.client.connection.pool.name.brief: The name of the connection pool; unique within the instrumented application. In case the connection pool implementation doesn't provide a name, instrumentation SHOULD use a combination of parameters that would make the name unique, for example, combining attributes `server.address`, `server.port`, and `db.namespace`, formatted as `server.address:server.port/db.namespace`. Instrumentations that generate connection pool name following different patterns SHOULD document it.

db.client.connection.state.brief: The state of a connection in the pool

db.collection.name.brief: The name of a collection (table, container) within the database.

db.command.name.brief: Name of the MongoDB command the span covers.

db.cosmosdb.operation_type.brief: Deprecated, no replacement at this time.

db.elasticsearch.schema_url.brief: OpenTelemetry semantic-convention schema URL the Elasticsearch client's own span attributes conform to.

db.instance.id.brief: Deprecated, no general replacement at this time. For Elasticsearch, use `db.elasticsearch.node.name` instead.

db.jdbc.driver_classname.brief: Removed, no replacement at this time.

db.mongodb.cursor_id.brief: Cursor id returned by the command.

db.mongodb.driver_connection_id.brief: Driver-local id of the connection the command was issued on.

db.mongodb.lsid.brief: Logical session id of the command, as JSON.

db.mongodb.server_connection_id.brief: Server-assigned id of the connection the command was issued on.

db.mssql.instance_name.brief: Deprecated, SQL Server instance is now populated as a part of `db.namespace` attribute.

db.namespace.brief: The database associated with the connection, fully qualified within the server address and port.

db.npgsql.connection_id.brief: Npgsql connector id the command ran on.

db.npgsql.data_source.brief: Name of the Npgsql data source the command ran on.

db.npgsql.prepared.brief: Whether the command was executed as a prepared statement.

db.npgsql.rows.brief: Number of rows the command returned or affected.

db.odp.connection.id.brief: Unique identifier of the ODP.NET connection, for diagnostic purposes.

db.odp.roundtrip.count.brief: Number of database server roundtrips the ODP.NET method makes.

db.odp.roundtrip.duration.brief: Database server roundtrip time, including ODP.NET processing, network send and receive, and database server processing.

db.odp.rows_affected.brief: Row count affected by the SQL DML statement.

db.odp.sql_id.brief: Oracle database SQL statement identifier, equivalent to SQL_ID.

db.odp.user.statement.brief: Redacted ODP.NET user-supplied command text, which can differ from the statement the database executes.

db.operation.batch.size.brief: The number of database operations included in a batch operation.

db.operation.name.brief: The name of the operation or command being executed.

db.operation.parameter.brief: A dynamic value in the URL path.

db.operation.summary.brief: Low-cardinality summary of the driver operation, spelled "<operation> <database>.<collection>".

db.query.parameter.brief: A database query parameter, with `<key>` being the parameter name, and the attribute value being a string representation of the parameter value.

db.query.summary.brief: Low cardinality summary of a database query.

db.response.returned_rows.brief: Number of rows returned by the operation.

db.response.status_code.brief: Database response code recorded as a string.

db.stored_procedure.name.brief: The name of a stored procedure within the database.

db.system.name.brief: The database management system (DBMS) product as identified by the client instrumentation.

db.user.brief: Deprecated, no replacement at this time.

destination.address.brief: Destination address - domain name if available without reverse DNS lookup; otherwise, IP address or UNIX domain socket name.

device.id.brief: A unique identifier representing the device

device.manufacturer.brief: The name of the device manufacturer

device.model.identifier.brief: The model identifier for the device

device.model.name.brief: The marketing name for the device model

dns.answers.brief: List of resolved IP addresses (for DNS lookup) or a single element containing domain name (for reverse lookup).

dns.question.name.brief: The domain name or an IP address being queried.

dotnet.gc.heap.generation.brief: Name of the garbage collector managed heap generation.

edge_group.delivered.brief: Whether the edge group delivered the message.

edge_group.delivery_status.brief: Why the edge group did or did not deliver the message, as `EdgeRunnerDeliveryStatus`.

edge_group.type.brief: The edge runner that delivered the message: DirectEdgeRunner, FanInEdgeRunner, FanOutEdgeRunner or ResponseEdgeRunner.

elastic.transport.attempted_nodes.brief: Number of nodes attempted during one logical operation.

elastic.transport.deserialize_response_m.brief: Milliseconds spent deserializing the HTTP response, recorded only above the transport's 20 ms threshold.

elastic.transport.prepare_request_ms.brief: Milliseconds spent preparing the HTTP request, recorded only above the transport's 20 ms threshold.

elastic.transport.product.name.brief: Name of the product library consuming Elastic.Transport.

elastic.transport.product.version.brief: Informational version of the product library consuming Elastic.Transport.

elastic.transport.schema_url.brief: Semantic-convention schema URL the transport layer's own attributes conform to.

elastic.transport.version.brief: Informational version of the Elastic.Transport library.

elasticsearch.node.name.brief: Represents the human-readable identifier of the node/instance to which a request was routed.

enduser.id.brief: Unique identifier of an end user in the system. It maybe a username, email address, or other identifier.

enduser.pseudo.id.brief: Pseudonymous identifier of an end user. This identifier should be a random value that is not directly linked or associated with the end user's actual identity.

enduser.scope.brief: Deprecated, no replacement at this time.

error.message.brief: A message providing more detail about an error in human-readable form.

error.type.brief: Describes a class of error the operation ended with.

event.name.brief: Identifies the class / type of event.

exception.escaped.brief: Indicates that the exception is escaping the scope of the span.

exception.stacktrace.brief: A stacktrace as a string in the natural representation for the language runtime. The representation is to be determined and documented by each language SIG.

exception.type.brief: The type of the exception (its fully-qualified class name, if applicable). The dynamic type of the exception should be preferred over the static type in languages that support it.

execution.result.brief: Result of the measured execution, reported by NServiceBus as "success" or "failure".

executor.id.brief: Id of the executor processing the message.

executor.input.brief: The message an executor received, serialized as JSON.

executor.output.brief: The output an executor produced, serialized as JSON.

executor.type.brief: Type name of the executor processing the message.

faas.coldstart.brief: A boolean that is true if the serverless function is executed for the first time (aka cold-start).

faas.cron.brief: A string containing the schedule period as [Cron Expression](https://docs.oracle.com/cd/E12058_01/doc/doc.1014/e12030/cron_expressions.htm).

faas.document.collection.brief: The name of the source on which the triggering operation was performed. For example, in Cloud Storage or S3 corresponds to the bucket name, and in Cosmos DB to the database name.

faas.document.name.brief: The document name/table subjected to the operation. For example, in Cloud Storage or S3 is the name of the file, and in Cosmos DB the table name.

faas.document.operation.brief: Describes the type of the operation that was performed on the data.

faas.document.time.brief: A string containing the time when the data was accessed in the [ISO 8601](https://www.iso.org/iso-8601-date-and-time-format.html) format expressed in [UTC](https://www.w3.org/TR/NOTE-datetime).

faas.instance.brief: The execution environment ID as a string, that will be potentially reused for other invocations to the same function/function version.

faas.invocation_id.brief: The invocation ID of the current function invocation.

faas.invoked_name.brief: The name of the invoked function.

faas.invoked_provider.brief: The cloud provider of the invoked function.

faas.invoked_region.brief: The cloud region of the invoked function.

faas.max_memory.brief: The amount of memory available to the serverless function converted to Bytes.

faas.name.brief: The name of the single function that this runtime instance executes.

faas.time.brief: A string containing the function invocation time in the [ISO 8601](https://www.iso.org/iso-8601-date-and-time-format.html) format expressed in [UTC](https://www.w3.org/TR/NOTE-datetime).

faas.trigger.brief: Type of the trigger which caused this function invocation.

faas.version.brief: The immutable version of the function being executed.

feature_flag.context.id.brief: The unique identifier for the flag evaluation context. For example, the targeting key.

feature_flag.error.message.brief: A message providing more detail about an error that occurred during feature flag evaluation in human-readable form.

feature_flag.key.brief: The lookup key of the feature flag.

feature_flag.result.reason.brief: The reason code which shows how a feature flag value was determined.

feature_flag.result.value.brief: The evaluated value of the feature flag.

feature_flag.result.variant.brief: A semantic identifier for an evaluated flag value.

feature_flag.set.id.brief: The identifier of the [flag set](https://openfeature.dev/specification/glossary/#flag-set) to which the feature flag belongs.

feature_flag.version.brief: The version of the ruleset used during the evaluation. This may be any stable value which uniquely identifies the ruleset.

file.accessed.brief: Time when the file was last accessed, in ISO 8601 format.

file.changed.brief: Time when the file attributes or metadata was last changed, in ISO 8601 format.

user_agent.name.brief: Name of the user-agent extracted from original. Usually refers to the browser's name.

user_agent.original.brief: Value of the [HTTP User-Agent](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9110.html#field.user-agent) header sent by the client.

user_agent.os.version.brief: The version string of the operating system as defined in [Version Attributes](/docs/resource/README.md#version-attributes).

user_agent.synthetic.type.brief: Specifies the category of synthetic traffic, such as tests or bots.

user_agent.version.brief: Version of the user-agent extracted from original. Usually refers to the browser's version

v8js.heap.space.name.brief: The name of the space type of heap memory.

v8js.resource.type.brief: The type of resource keeping the event loop active.

vcs.change.id.brief: The ID of the change (pull request/merge request/changelist) if applicable. This is usually a unique (within repository) identifier generated by the VCS system.

vcs.change.state.brief: The state of the change (pull request/merge request/changelist).

vcs.change.title.brief: The human readable title of the change (pull request/merge request/changelist). This title is often a brief summary of the change and may get merged in to a ref as the commit summary.

vcs.line_change.type.brief: The type of line change being measured on a branch or change.

vcs.owner.name.brief: The group owner within the version control system.

vcs.provider.name.brief: The name of the version control system provider.

vcs.ref.base.name.brief: The name of the [reference](https://git-scm.com/docs/gitglossary#def_ref) such as **branch** or **tag** in the repository.

vcs.ref.base.revision.brief: The revision, literally [revised version](https://www.merriam-webster.com/dictionary/revision), The revision most often refers to a commit object in Git, or a revision number in SVN.

vcs.ref.base.type.brief: The type of the [reference](https://git-scm.com/docs/gitglossary#def_ref) in the repository.

vcs.ref.head.name.brief: The name of the [reference](https://git-scm.com/docs/gitglossary#def_ref) such as **branch** or **tag** in the repository.

vcs.ref.head.revision.brief: The revision, literally [revised version](https://www.merriam-webster.com/dictionary/revision), The revision most often refers to a commit object in Git, or a revision number in SVN.

vcs.ref.head.type.brief: The type of the [reference](https://git-scm.com/docs/gitglossary#def_ref) in the repository.

vcs.ref.type.brief: The type of the [reference](https://git-scm.com/docs/gitglossary#def_ref) in the repository.

vcs.repository.name.brief: The human readable name of the repository. It SHOULD NOT include any additional identifier like Group/SubGroup in GitLab or organization in GitHub.

vcs.repository.url.full.brief: The [canonical URL](https://support.google.com/webmasters/answer/10347851) of the repository providing the complete HTTP(S) address in order to locate and identify the repository through a browser.

wcf.channel.path.brief: Local path of the URI the channel that received the request listens on.

wcf.channel.scheme.brief: URI scheme of the channel that received the request.

webengine.description.brief: Additional description of the web engine (e.g. detailed version and edition information).

webengine.name.brief: The name of the web engine.

webengine.version.brief: The version of the web engine.

workflow.definition.brief: The workflow's executors and edges, serialized as JSON.

workflow.id.brief: Id of the workflow, which Microsoft.Agents.AI.Workflows 1.24.0 takes from its start executor.

zos.smf.id.brief: The System Management Facility (SMF) Identifier uniquely identified a z/OS system within a SYSPLEX or mainframe environment and is used for system and performance analysis.

zos.sysplex.name.brief: The name of the SYSPLEX to which the z/OS system belongs too.
